item.title: Mixed fortunes for the Basketball teams of the region
item.description: In the Womens Super league, Mc Evoys Cavan Eagles suffered a loss on their travels at the weekend as they went down by 75 points to 82 to FloMAX Liffey Celtics. The Breffni side sit 8th in the table on 21 points. It was better news in the Mens first Division as Carrick Cruisers registered a 90 points to 83 win away to Killarney Cougars. That result moved the Monaghan representatives up to 5th in the table on 39 points. Advertisement

item.title: Cavan hurlers back in promotion hunt
item.description: Cavan hurling manager Ollie Bellew says his side got off to a flyer in Saturdays league win over Lancashire. They ran out five point winners in Saturdays meeting to keep up their promotion hopes in Division 4 but he feels his side have improvements to make based off their second half showing. Next up for Cavan is a trip away to Leitrim on Saturday with the hosts having accounted for Monaghan at the weekend Advertisement

item.title: Kayleigh Trappe launches Batteries for Barretstown 2026
item.description: Co Monaghan influencer and TV personality Kayleigh Trappe has lent her support to the launch of the 2026 Batteries for Barretstown Schools Challenge. The scheme was launched by European Recycling Platform (ERP), Ireland’s only pan-European compliance scheme for Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) and waste batteries. item.title: Man charged over death of Michael Gaine
item.description: A man's been charged in connection with the death of Michael Gaine. The 56-year-old farmer was reported missing last March - human tissue found on his farm nearly two months later was confirmed to be his. Gardai yesterday arrested a man in his 50s as part of the investigation. He's been charged and is due before Tralee District Court this afternoon. Advertisement

item.title: New Garda Station in Bailieboro will open in April
item.description: Minister Niamh Smyth has received confirmation from the Minister for Public Expenditure that the new Garda Station in Bailieboro will open in April. She said she received the good news that the station will be complete in April at which point Gardaí will commence the occupation of the building. It's envisaged that over 60 Gardaí and civilians will work from this building once fully operational. item.title: Local farmer describes treatment of Bord Bia protestors
item.description: A local farmer is angry with the treatment of protestors inside of the Bord Bia buildings. Monaghan farmer Frank Brady is calling for a resolution to the situation to be reached. A demonstration against the chairperson of Bord Bia, Larry Murrin will take place in Co. Cavan tonight. item.title: Peace project launched in Monaghan
item.description: The launch of a peace programme took place at Monaghan Peace Campus today. This €2.08 million project, supported by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB), will see over 3,400 people from NI and the border regions of Ireland, benefit from grassroot projects in community leadership, community festivals and media initiatives. item.title: Man charged with murder of Kerry farmer Michael Gaine
item.description: A 54-year-old man has been charged with the murder of Michael Gaine in county Kerry. Michael Kelley, of Chapel Street, Tralee appeared at Tralee District Court this afternoon. Detective Sgt Mark O’Sullivan told the court Michael Kelley made no reply to the charge of murdering Michael Gaine on a date unknown between the 20th and 21st of March 2025.
